skill.name: incident-runbook-templates
skill.description: Templates for incident response runbooks covering detection, triage, mitigation, recovery, escalation, and communication.
skill.summary: Create incident response runbooks for service outages, database incidents, escalation, and stakeholder updates.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All static findings are documentation artifacts in SKILL.md, including Markdown code fences, inline examples, sample URLs, sample CIDR values, and /dev/null usage. I found no executable scripts, prompt injection text, credential handling, hidden network behavior, or data exfiltration intent.

remediation.issue: Production-impacting commands appear in example runbooks.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit guidance that examples require environment validation and human approval before execution.

remediation.issue: Sample URLs and CIDR ranges could be copied without customization.
remediation.suggestion: Replace hardcoded sample hosts, internal endpoints, and CIDR ranges with clear placeholders.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md references resources/implementation-playbook.md, but the package only includes SKILL.md.
remediation.suggestion: Include the referenced playbook or remove the instruction that points to it.

content.value_statement: Incident teams need clear procedures before production issues start. This skill provides structured runbook templates for triage, mitigation, recovery, escalation, and communication.
actual_capabilities: Creates service outage runbook structures with impact, detection, triage, mitigation, verification, and escalation sections.
Provides severity levels and response-time examples for incident classification.
Supplies templates for internal notifications, status updates, and resolution messages.
Includes database incident guidance for connection pools, replication lag, locks, and disk space issues.
Connects runbooks to dashboards, alerts, rollback steps, and post-incident review practices.
limitations: Examples are generic and require validation against the user environment.
The skill does not execute remediation commands or verify infrastructure state.
The package only includes SKILL.md, so the referenced implementation playbook is not present.
It does not replace incident commander, security, legal, or compliance approval.

use_cases.title: Create Baseline On-Call Runbooks
use_cases.description: Draft consistent incident procedures for services that lack documented response steps.

use_cases.title: Customize Service Outage Response
use_cases.description: Adapt triage, mitigation, rollback, and verification steps for a specific production service.

use_cases.title: Standardize Incident Communication
use_cases.description: Prepare escalation paths, stakeholder updates, and resolution notices for response teams.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Runbook
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a first incident response document.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an incident runbook for [service name]. Include severity, impact, alerts, first triage steps, mitigation, rollback, verification, escalation, and communication sections.

prompt_templates.title: Customize an Outage Runbook
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a service-specific outage plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the service outage template for [service]. Use these alerts: [alerts]. Use these dashboards: [dashboards]. Include safe rollback and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Database Incident Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for database-focused response procedures.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a database incident runbook for [database system]. Cover connection exhaustion, replication lag, locks, disk pressure, escalation, customer impact, and recovery validation.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Existing Incident Runbooks
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request to improve an existing operational process.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this runbook: [paste runbook]. Identify missing triage data, unsafe assumptions, unclear owners, weak rollback steps, missing verification, and communication gaps.

output_examples.input: Need a SEV2 payment service runbook.
output: A service overview with owners, channels, expected impact, and severity criteria.
Detection and triage sections that reference alerts, dashboards, dependency checks, and recent deployments.
Mitigation, rollback, verification, escalation, and update templates for the response team.

output_examples.input: Need guidance for database connection pool exhaustion.
output: A triage flow for connection counts, active sessions, long-running work, and application behavior.
Mitigation options that separate safe checks from production-impacting actions.
Verification steps for restored capacity, normal latency, and incident follow-up.

output_examples.input: Need an incident status update for leaders.
output_examples.output: A concise update with severity, status, customer impact, actions taken, next steps, owner, and next update time.

best_practices: Replace placeholder services, dashboards, CIDRs, and contacts with verified environment values.
Require explicit human approval before production-impacting commands are executed.
Review and test runbooks after incidents, simulations, or major architecture changes.
anti_patterns: Copying example commands into production without checking scope, permissions, or rollback impact.
Leaving escalation contacts, dashboards, and ownership fields blank.
Using one generic runbook for every service without service-specific dependencies and alerts.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates structured incident runbooks for outages, database issues, escalation, recovery, and communication.

faq.question: Does the skill run commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides templates and examples. Users must approve and execute any operational command themselves.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it help during an active incident?
faq.answer: Yes, but teams should validate every step against current system state and response authority.

faq.question: What should I customize first?
faq.answer: Customize service names, owners, alerts, dashboards, rollback steps, dependencies, escalation contacts, and verification checks.

faq.question: Does it replace formal incident policy?
faq.answer: No. It supports documentation and response planning, but does not replace approved security or compliance procedures.
